title: CLI
text: kroma.cli CLI kroma run starts one experiment. With no arguments, kroma prints help and exits. On this page Command Flags From Python Command kroma run \ --method_config kroma_scibert_envo_sweet \ --llm meta-llama/Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct-Turbo-Free \ --baseline --method_config is the JSONL file name under experiments/configs/method/<llm>/ . --llm is that directory name. Both are required. Source: cli.py . Flags Flag Meaning --method_config Required. Config name, without .jsonl . --llm Required. Model directory under experiments/configs/method/ . --size Fraction of the alignment to score. Default full . --baseline Single-model baseline. --debate Several agents, several rounds. Omit it for one model. --reasoning Ask the model to reason before yes or no. --active_learning Hold low-confidence pairs for review. --compare_models Compare model settings from the config. --bisim Use the bisimulation context path. From Python RunCommand(args).execute() -> None RunCommand imports MatchingRun and runs it. If a model package is missing, it exits with the install line uv pip install '.[models]' . title: Ontology matching with knowledge retrieval and large language models
text: Ontology matching with knowledge retrieval and large language models KROMA matches concepts across two ontologies. These pages are the Python API: what you call, and what it returns. $ git clone https://github.com/lamng3/kroma.git && cd kroma $ ./setup.sh && source .venv/bin/activate $ kroma run --help Matching run CLI Paper What KROMA asks the model real prompts , recorded answers Try it: Pick a pair to see the prompt KROMA sends for it, and how the recorded run answered. Mouse–Human anatomy pairs. The prompt is built by KROMA's own loader and build_task_prompt from the two ontologies. The answer is what the routed run in the Agentic Ontologist recorded for the pair, and the tier that settled it: an evidence-only answer never reached a model. The page asks no model. A run loads an alignment, retrieves local context for each concept, asks a language model whether the pair matches, and refines the joined graph. The command line is the usual entry. The same steps are available as functions. The pieces CLI kroma run and the flags that select a config, a model, and a mode. Matching run MatchingRun prepares the task, scores pairs, and writes metrics. Loaders CSV alignments and an OWL class hierarchy. Query Parents, children, synonyms, and labels from a named source. Models OpenAI and Together chat models, and embedding backends. Retrieval Cosine search over concatenated text and Node2Vec vectors. Refinement Online updates while scoring, and a final offline collapse. Metrics Precision, recall, and F1 for a binary alignment. One run kroma run parses flags and calls MatchingRun.execute . prepare reads the method JSONL and the dataset JSON, then builds vector stores. score_pairs retrieves context, calls infer , and records the prediction. finish runs offline_refine and writes a metrics JSON file. Install git clone https://github.com/lamng3/kroma.git cd kroma ./setup.sh source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install ".[models]" Copy .env.example to .env and set TOGETHERAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_API_KEY . The paper is ISWC 2025 .

title: Leaderboard
text: Results Leaderboard KROMA's F1 on six tracks, ranked against the best published baseline, its own ablations, and smaller or cheaper models. KROMA has the highest F1 on all six tracks in the paper. The board also shows what each part of it contributes: removing knowledge retrieval or ontology refinement lowers F1 on every track reported, and with a small model it still beats the best baseline on some tracks. How to read it F1 (%) is the alignment's F1 against the reference matches, as published (Table 3 of the paper). KROMA rows use Llama-3.3-70B unless a tag says otherwise. Ablation rows remove retrieval or refinement. Baseline is the best of MILA, OLaLa, and LLM4OM on that track, with their reported models. These are published numbers, not a run of this site. The paper has the protocol. Previous Metrics

title: Loaders
text: kroma.tasks.loader Loaders A loader returns a source graph, a target graph, and a list of alignments. On this page OntologyLoader CSV alignments OWL OntologyLoader load() -> (source_graph, target_graph, alignments) An alignment is (source, target, label) . Each endpoint is a (label, uri) pair. Source: loader.py . CSV alignments CsvAlignmentLoader(csv_paths, dataset="ncit-doid").load() For ncit-doid , rows use src_code , src_ety , tgt_code , tgt_ety , tgt_cands , and score . Other datasets use source , source_uri , target , target_uri , and relation . OWL OwlOntologyLoader(owl_path).load() This reads an OWL or RDF/XML file and builds the class hierarchy from rdfs:subClassOf , with synonyms from the annotation properties on each class. title: Metrics
text: kroma.metrics.scoring Metrics Metrics are binary. A positive prediction that matches the label is a true positive. On this page Call Empty input Call calculate_metrics(y_true, y_pred, positive_label=1) -> (precision, recall, f1) y_true and y_pred are sequences of labels, zipped in order. positive_label defaults to 1 . Source: scoring.py . Empty input Precision is 0 when there are no positive predictions. Recall is 0 when there are no positive labels. F1 is 0 when precision and recall are both 0. The function does not raise on an empty pair of lists. Previous Refinement Next Leaderboard

title: Models
text: kroma.inference Models Chat providers adapt OpenAI and Together. Embedding providers adapt Hugging Face and sentence-transformers. On this page Factories Inference Factories create_inference_model(backend, model_name) -> BaseModel create_embedding_model(backend, model_name) -> BaseEmbeddingModel register_chat_backend(name, provider_cls) -> None register_embedding_backend(name, provider_cls) -> None Chat backends are openai and togetherai . The API key is OPENAI_API_KEY or TOGETHERAI_API_KEY . Embedding backends are huggingface and sentence-transformers . BaseModel.generate retries transient connection, timeout, and rate-limit errors. Source: factory.py . Inference infer(debate, backend, model_name, source_term, target_term, ...) -> prediction, metrics, confidence, accept Class Role SingleModelInference One agent, one round. DebateInference One agent per config, for n_rounds rounds. expand_term calls query and returns the concept code plus parents, children, synonyms, and labels. Source: inference.py . title: Matching run
text: kroma.pipeline Matching run MatchingRun is the template for one evaluation: prepare, score, then finish. On this page Call Methods Output Call MatchingRun(args, listener=None) MatchingRun.execute() -> dict execute calls prepare , score_pairs , and finish . listener defaults to MetricsListener , which counts tokens and refinement time. Source: pipeline.py . Methods Method What it does prepare() Load the method JSONL and dataset JSON, open output files, build the task, and fill the vector stores. score_pairs() Judge each alignment. Skip a pair already stored. Refine on a fixed interval. finish() Run the final offline refinement and write the metrics JSON. Output Accepted alignments go under results/ . Pairs that need an expert go under reviews/ . The metrics file sits next to the prediction file and ends in .metrics.json . It includes precision, recall, F1, token counts, and refinement timings. The run log is logs/kroma.log . Previous CLI Next Loaders

title: Query
text: kroma.tasks.query_engine Query query asks each named strategy for local context and concatenates the results. On this page Call Strategies Call query(concept_code, pcmap, dictionary, options) -> parents, children, synonyms, labels register_query_strategy(name, strategy) -> None Unknown option names are skipped. A strategy that raises is skipped, and the other options still return. Source: query_engine.py . Strategies Strategy Option names DictionaryStrategy envo , sweet , mouse , human , yago , wikidata , mi , mi2 , matonto , emmo , omim , ordo SparqlStrategy ncit , doid , dbpedia OntologyStrategy ontology ConceptNetStrategy conceptnet A custom source is any object with fetch(code, pcmap, dictionary, topk) registered under a name. title: Refinement
text: kroma.algorithms.refinement Refinement Refinement keeps the joined graph consistent while pairs are accepted, then collapses it at the end. On this page Online Offline Online online_refine(full_graph, rank_attr, equiv_classes, delta_edges, pred) -> (equiv_classes, expert_questions) New edges are added to the graph. The function returns the updated equivalence classes and the pairs that should go to an expert. ReviewRepository records those questions. PredictionRepository appends accepted rows. Offline offline_refine(adj, rank_attr) -> dict compute_node_ranks assigns each node its longest distance from a root. offline_refine partitions nodes by that rank, splits blocks that a higher node separates, and collapses each block. MatchingRun.finish calls this once after scoring. Source: refinement.py . Previous Retrieval Next Metrics

title: Retrieval
text: kroma.retrieval Retrieval Retrieval ranks concepts by cosine similarity of a combined text and structure vector. On this page VectorStore Combined embeddings VectorStore VectorStore.add(ext_ids, embeddings) -> None VectorStore.query(query_emb, top_k=5) -> list[(id, score)] add stacks embedding rows and keeps the external ids in the same order. query L2-normalizes the stored matrix and the query, then returns the top cosine scores. An empty store returns an empty list. Source: vector_store.py . Combined embeddings compute_combined_embeddings( adj_dict, node_keys, text_embs, n2v_kwargs=None, combine_method="concat", alpha=0.5, ) The default combine method is concatenation of the text embedding and the Node2Vec embedding. alpha applies when the method is a weighted mix rather than concatenation. Source: node2vec.py . Previous Models Next Refinement
